title: A gym with under 8 weeks of check-ins is shown as busy too easily
what: The member app's 'how busy is the gym' compares the last 90 minutes with what is usual at that time. For a gym with less than 8 weeks of check-in history, the usual figure is always divided by one week too many (a gym with 1 week and 1 day of history divides one week's count by 2), so 'usual' comes out a half to an eighth too low. The gym then shows 'busy' when it is only normal, and 'normal' when it is quiet. Every new gym goes through this for its first 8 weeks.
expected: The usual figure is averaged only over the weeks that really have check-ins, so a new gym's busy level means the same as an older gym's.
how_often: every new gym, for its first 8 weeks of check-ins
fix_line: Count only the weeks that lie after the first check-in when working out the usual level

title: A member who joins today brings 30 days of workouts done before joining onto the gym's leaderboard and challenge
what: The member's phone sends its last 30 days of workouts and the server counts all of them, with no check against the day the member joined this gym. Someone who joins today (or moves from another gym) can go straight into the top 10, and in a running challenge their workouts from before they joined count toward the goal, so they can win the free days on the day they join. The owner's confirm list shows only the number, not that most of it came before joining.
expected: Only workouts on or after the day the member joined this gym count on its leaderboard and in its challenges.
how_often: every member who joins or moves gym while active
fix_line: Leave out days before the member joined this gym when adding up the leaderboard and challenge totals

A drop in friends joined (enquiry deleted) shows no reason, already covered as untested by FN-A8-phone-shop-2-3-07.

Leaderboard rows and your place come from one rows function; the members count beside it from the same 30 days. Challenge: my value and hitters from the same days and goal. Busy: level and week bars from the same check-in list.
Busy level (averaged over 'weeks') and week bars (raw 8-week counts) treat a short or gappy history differently: the level is skewed, the bars are not.
